copy.blurb:
FIFA World Cup 2026 on Sunday, overnight UTC kickoff, brings Ecuador and Curaçao together. The Desk's read disagrees with the market on the Curaçao side, by +7.6pp — and that disagreement is the Pick.

The Elo prior reads Ecuador 1790 vs Curaçao 1480: 310 points in favour of Ecuador, which is a meaningful but not decisive prior. Both Elo numbers are pulled live from the public Elo source. The adjustment layer is quiet on this fixture — no host bonus, no home-ground correction, no altitude folding in. The Elo numbers above are what the model uses.

Three-way split from the model: Ecuador to win at 76%, the draw at 11%, and Curaçao to win at 13%. The away side reads 13% on this distribution — the model's central case for Curaçao.

On the same three-way, Polymarket: Ecuador to win at 78%, the draw at 16%, and Curaçao to win at 5%. Polymarket has Curaçao at 5%, which prices out at American odds of +1861; the model has the same side at 13%. The +7.6pp gap across them is the disagreement we're surfacing.

The +3pp Pick threshold isn't on the point estimate, it's on the 5th-percentile from a 100-sample bootstrap of the Elo prior plus bonuses. On Curaçao, that haircut lands the model at 9%; the market is at 5%. Even on the conservative reading, the gap is +4.2pp. The engine isn't arguing reputation, recency, or narrative. It's reading the underlying numbers and finding Curaçao priced shorter on the market than the prior supports — that's the disagreement.

What would close this gap: confirmed team news that pulls the prior down on the side we like, a venue or weather change, or a tournament suspension landing before kickoff. With kickoff 25 days out, refresh is weekly; daily cadence picks up inside the final five days. A Pick this wide doesn't collapse on small news; a narrow one can flip to Pass on a single refresh. Either way, the engine republishes and the page reflects the latest read.
drivers: This is a selection call on the Curaçao side, not a blanket read on the market.
Confirmed XI, fitness news, and weather re-enter the prior closer to kickoff.
Bootstrap lower-bound on the Curaçao side still clears the Pick threshold.
Editorial analysis only — Odds Primer does not place trades or recommend a wager.
copy.summary: This is a Pick on the Curaçao side — the model has them at 13%, the market at 5%. A +7.6pp gap is enough on a fixture this close to even.
